1	I have all the source material now. Producing the reconstruction-grade spec document.

3	# Naming & Branding
4	
5	## Name: Monokl
6	
7	**Monokl** (pronounced "MON-oh-kl") is an invented word derived from *monocle* — a single precision lens used for close examination. The name reflects the tool's purpose: examining code structure with precision and clarity.
8	
9	- **Crate name:** `monokl` (formerly `loupe`)
10	- **Package name:** `stubhub-monokl`
11	- **CLI binary:** `monokl`
12	- **Short command alias:** `mnkl`
13	- **npm wrapper:** `@stubhub/monokl`
14	- **Cache directory:** `.monokl/`
15	
16	### Rationale
17	The name was chosen after an exhaustive search for a name that:
18	- Evokes precision optical examination (monocle, loupe family)
19	- Has no trademark conflicts (USPTO, EUIPO, crates.io, npm)
20	- Has no negative linguistic associations in major languages
21	- Is short, pronounceable across languages, and memorable
22	- Is ownable and registerable as a brand
23	- Carries a Rust/systems-tool feel
24	
25	The `k` substitution (monocle → monokl) makes the name distinctive and technically flavored, consistent with the Rust ecosystem aesthetic (cf. `tokei`, `zoxide`, `hyperfine`). In several Slavic languages (Russian, Czech, Slovak, Polish), "monokl" is the standard word for monocle — a bonus rather than a conflict.
26	
27	### Trademark & Namespace Status
28	- ✅ No USPTO trademark conflict found
29	- ✅ No EUIPO trademark conflict found
30	- ✅ `crates.io/crates/monokl` — unclaimed (reserve immediately on first publish)
31	- ✅ `npmjs.com/package/monokl` — verify and claim
32	- ✅ No industry developer tool conflicts found
33	- ⚠️ File USPTO Class 9 + Class 42 trademark application before public launch

622	```rust
623	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
624	pub enum Token {
625	    Plus,
626	    Minus,
627	    RegexPrefix,
628	    QuotedString(String),
629	    Word(String),
630	    Eof,
631	}
632	
633	pub struct Lexer<'a> {
634	    input: &'a str,
635	    pos: usize,
636	}
637	
638	impl<'a> Lexer<'a> {
639	    pub fn new(input: &'a str) -> Self {
640	        Self { input, pos: 0 }
641	    }
642	
643	    fn remaining(&self) -> &str {
644	        &self.input[self.pos..]
645	    }
646	
647	    fn peek(&self) -> Option<char> {
648	        self.remaining().chars().next()
649	    }
650	
651	    fn advance(&mut self) -> Option<char> {
652	        let ch = self.peek()?;
653	        self.pos += ch.len_utf8();
654	        Some(ch)
655	    }
656	
657	    fn skip_whitespace(&mut self) {
658	        while let Some(ch) = self.peek() {
659	            if ch.is_ascii_whitespace() {
660	                self.pos += ch.len_utf8();
661	            } else {
662	                break;
663	            }
664	        }
665	    }
666	
667	    fn read_word(&mut self) -> String {
668	        let mut s = String::new();
669	        loop {
670	            match self.peek() {
671	                None => break,
672	                Some(ch) if ch.is_ascii_whitespace() => break,
673	                Some(ch) => {
674	                    s.push(ch);
675	                    self.pos += ch.len_utf8();
676	                }
677	            }
678	        }
679	        s
680	    }
681	
682	    fn read_quoted(&mut self) -> String {
683	        let mut s = String::new();
684	        loop {
685	            match self.advance() {
686	                None | Some('"') => break,
687	                Some('\\') => {
688	                    match self.peek() {
689	                        Some('"') => {
690	                            self.pos += 1;
691	                            s.push('"');
692	                        }
693	                        _ => s.push('\\'),
694	                    }
695	                }
696	                Some(ch) => s.push(ch),
697	            }
698	        }
699	        s
700	    }
701	
702	    pub fn next_token(&mut self) -> Token {
703	        self.skip_whitespace();
704	        match self.peek() {
705	            None => Token::Eof,
706	            Some('+') => { self.pos += 1; Token::Plus }
707	            Some('-') => { self.pos += 1; Token::Minus }
708	            Some('"') => { self.pos += 1; Token::QuotedString(self.read_quoted()) }
709	            Some(_) => {
710	                if self.remaining().starts_with("regex:") {
711	                    self.pos += "regex:".len();
712	                    Token::RegexPrefix
713	                } else {
714	                    Token::Word(self.read_word())
715	                }
716	            }
717	        }
718	    }
719	}
720	```
721	
722	Rules: `+`/`-` consumed as Token::Plus/Token::Minus only when they begin a term (`read_word` greedily consumes everything except whitespace). `regex:` (case-sensitive) emits RegexPrefix, the next token is the pattern. `\"` is the only recognized escape in quoted strings.

727	use super::lexer::{Lexer, Token};
728	use crate::error::{MonoklError, Result};
729	
730	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
731	pub enum Modifier {
732	    Required,
733	    Excluded,
734	    Optional,
735	}
736	
737	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
738	pub struct ParsedTerm {
739	    pub modifier: Modifier,
740	    pub pattern: String,
741	    pub is_regex: bool,
742	}
743	
744	pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<ParsedTerm>> {
745	    const LIMIT: usize = 64;
746	    if input.trim().is_empty() {
747	        return Ok(Vec::new());
748	    }
749	    let mut lexer = Lexer::new(input);
750	    let mut terms: Vec<ParsedTerm> = Vec::new();
751	    loop {
752	        let tok = lexer.next_token();
753	        match tok {
754	            Token::Eof => break,
755	            Token::Plus => {
756	                let content = lexer.next_token();
757	                if let Some(term) = content_to_term(content, Modifier::Required) {
758	                    terms.push(term);
759	                }
760	            }
761	            Token::Minus => {
762	                let content = lexer.next_token();
763	                if let Some(term) = content_to_term(content, Modifier::Excluded) {
764	                    terms.push(term);
765	                }
766	            }
767	            Token::RegexPrefix => {
768	                let pattern_tok = lexer.next_token();
769	                match pattern_tok {
770	                    Token::Word(raw) | Token::QuotedString(raw) => {
771	                        terms.push(ParsedTerm {
772	                            modifier: Modifier::Optional,
773	                            pattern: raw,
774	                            is_regex: true,
775	                        });
776	                    }
777	                    _ => {}
778	                }
779	            }
780	            Token::Word(w) => {
781	                terms.push(ParsedTerm {
782	                    modifier: Modifier::Optional,
783	                    pattern: regex::escape(&w),
784	                    is_regex: false,
785	                });
786	            }
787	            Token::QuotedString(s) => {
788	                terms.push(ParsedTerm {
789	                    modifier: Modifier::Optional,
790	                    pattern: regex::escape(&s),
791	                    is_regex: false,
792	                });
793	            }
794	        }
795	    }
796	    if terms.len() > LIMIT {
797	        return Err(MonoklError::TooManyTerms {
798	            count: terms.len(),
799	            limit: LIMIT,
800	        });
801	    }
802	    Ok(terms)
803	}
804	
805	fn content_to_term(tok: Token, modifier: Modifier) -> Option<ParsedTerm> {
806	    match tok {
807	        Token::Word(w) => Some(ParsedTerm {
808	            modifier,
809	            pattern: regex::escape(&w),
810	            is_regex: false,
811	        }),
812	        Token::QuotedString(s) => Some(ParsedTerm {
813	            modifier,
814	            pattern: regex::escape(&s),
815	            is_regex: false,
816	        }),
817	        Token::RegexPrefix => None, // `+regex:foo` documented as silently losing modifier
818	        _ => None,
819	    }
820	}
821	```

823	Limit: `const LIMIT: usize = 64`. Whitespace-only input returns an empty vec without error.

867	static STOP_WORDS: &[&str] = &[
868	    "the","and","for","are","but","not","you","all","can","had","her","was","one","our",
869	    "out","day","get","has","him","his","how","its","may","new","now","old","see","two",
870	    "use","way","who","did","let","put","too","any",
871	    // common code stop words
872	    "fn","var","const","mut","pub","use","mod","impl","type","enum","struct","trait",
873	    "return","import","export","from","default","class","extends","interface",
874	];
875	
876	pub fn tokenize(input: &str) -> Vec<String> {
877	    let mut result = Vec::new();
878	    let chars: Vec<char> = input.chars().collect();
879	    if chars.is_empty() { return result; }
880	    let mut current_word = String::new();
881	    for idx in 0..chars.len() {
882	        let ch = chars[idx];
883	        if ch == '_' || ch == '-' || !ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
884	            if !current_word.is_empty() {
885	                result.push(current_word.clone());
886	                current_word.clear();
887	            }
888	            continue;
889	        }
890	        let should_break = if idx > 0 {
891	            let prev_ch = chars[idx - 1];
892	            if prev_ch.is_ascii_lowercase() && ch.is_ascii_uppercase() {
893	                true
894	            } else if prev_ch.is_ascii_uppercase() && ch.is_ascii_uppercase() {
895	                idx + 1 < chars.len() && chars[idx + 1].is_ascii_lowercase()
896	            } else if prev_ch.is_ascii_uppercase() && ch.is_ascii_lowercase() {
897	                false
898	            } else if prev_ch.is_ascii_alphabetic() && ch.is_ascii_digit() {
899	                false
900	            } else if prev_ch.is_ascii_digit() && ch.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
901	                true
902	            } else {
903	                false
904	            }
905	        } else {
906	            false
907	        };
908	        if should_break && !current_word.is_empty() {
909	            result.push(current_word.clone());
910	            current_word.clear();
911	        }
912	        current_word.push(ch.to_ascii_lowercase());
913	    }
914	    if !current_word.is_empty() { result.push(current_word); }
915	    result.into_iter()
916	        .filter(|token| token.len() >= 2 && !STOP_WORDS.contains(&token.as_str()))
917	        .collect()
918	}
919	
920	pub fn tokenize_source(source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
921	    let mut result = Vec::new();
922	    let mut current_fragment = String::new();
923	    for ch in source.chars() {
924	        if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '_' {
925	            current_fragment.push(ch);
926	        } else if !current_fragment.is_empty() {
927	            let tokens = tokenize(&current_fragment);
928	            result.extend(tokens);
929	            current_fragment.clear();
930	        }
931	    }
932	    if !current_fragment.is_empty() {
933	        let tokens = tokenize(&current_fragment);
934	        result.extend(tokens);
935	    }
936	    result
937	}

940	Split transitions: lower→UPPER breaks; UPPER→UPPER breaks only if next char is lowercase (handles "XMLParser" → "xml","parser"); UPPER→lower never breaks; letter→digit doesn't break (keeps "v8"); digit→letter breaks. Filter: token.len() >= 2 AND not in STOP_WORDS. `tokenize_source` preserves duplicates for BM25 TF.

945	use std::collections::BTreeMap;
946	use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};

952	
953	pub fn search_files(
954	    root: &Utf8Path,
955	    patterns: &[&str],
956	    allow_tests: bool,
957	    no_gitignore: bool,
958	    max_candidates: usize,
959	) -> Result<BTreeMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<LineHit>>> {
960	    let combined = patterns.join("|");
961	    let matcher = RegexMatcherBuilder::new().case_insensitive(true).build(&combined)?;
962	    let walk = WalkBuilder::new(root)
963	        .standard_filters(!no_gitignore)
964	        .build();
965	    let mut results: BTreeMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<LineHit>> = BTreeMap::new();
966	    let mut candidate_count = 0usize;
967	    for entry in walk {
968	        let entry = entry.map_err(|e| crate::error::MonoklError::Walk {
969	            path: root.to_owned(),
970	            source: e,
971	        })?;
972	        if !entry.file_type().is_some_and(|t| t.is_file()) { continue; }
973	        let path = match Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(entry.into_path()) {
974	            Ok(p) => p,
975	            Err(_non_utf8) => continue,
976	        };
977	        if !allow_tests && is_test_path(&path) { continue; }
978	        if candidate_count >= max_candidates { break; }
979	        let mut hits: Vec<LineHit> = Vec::new();
980	        let mut searcher = SearcherBuilder::new().build();
981	        if let Err(e) = searcher.search_path(
982	            &matcher,
983	            path.as_std_path(),
984	            UTF8(|line_number, line| {
985	                #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
986	                hits.push(LineHit {
987	                    line_number: line_number as usize,
988	                    text: line.trim_end_matches('\n').to_owned(),
989	                });
990	                Ok(true)
991	            }),
992	        ) {
993	            tracing::warn!("search_path error on {path}: {e}");
994	            continue;
995	        }
996	        if !hits.is_empty() {
997	            candidate_count += 1;
998	            results.insert(path, hits);
999	        }
1000	    }
1001	    Ok(results)
1002	}

1008	        || s.contains("/tests/")
1009	        || s.contains("/spec/")
1010	        || s.ends_with(".test.ts")
1011	        || s.ends_with(".test.tsx")

1048	        let cov = boost::coverage_boost(&block);
1049	        let ntype = boost::node_type_boost(block.node_kind);
1050	        let final_score = round6(bm25 * ntype + cov);
1051	        RankedBlock {

1054	            coverage_boost: cov,
1055	            node_type_boost: ntype,
1056	            final_score,

1058	            parent_context: None,

1062	        b.final_score.partial_cmp(&a.final_score).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
1063	    });
1064	    for (i, block) in ranked.iter_mut().enumerate() { block.rank = i + 1; }

1074	const K1: f64 = 1.5;
1075	const B: f64 = 0.5;
1076	const DP: f64 = 1_000_000.0;
1077	
1078	pub fn round6(x: f64) -> f64 {
1079	    (x * DP).round() / DP
1080	}
1081	
1082	#[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]
1083	pub fn score<S: std::hash::BuildHasher>(
1084	    doc_tokens: &[String],
1085	    query_terms: &[&str],
1086	    avg_doc_len: f64,
1087	    corpus_size: usize,
1088	    df: &std::collections::HashMap<String, usize, S>,
1089	) -> f64 {
1090	    if query_terms.is_empty() || doc_tokens.is_empty() { return 0.0; }
1091	    let doc_len = doc_tokens.len() as f64;
1092	    let n = corpus_size as f64;
1093	    let mut total_score = 0.0;
1094	    for term in query_terms {
1095	        let df_t = df.get(*term).copied().unwrap_or(0) as f64;
1096	        let tf = doc_tokens.iter().filter(|t| t == term).count() as f64;
1097	        if tf == 0.0 { continue; }
1098	        let idf = ((n - df_t + 0.5) / (df_t + 0.5) + 1.0).ln();
1099	        let norm_factor = K1 * (1.0 - B + B * (doc_len / avg_doc_len));
1100	        let tf_norm = (tf * (K1 + 1.0)) / (tf + norm_factor);
1101	        total_score += idf * tf_norm;
1102	    }
1103	    round6(total_score)
1104	}
1105	```
1106	
1107	Constants: `K1=1.5`, `B=0.5`, `DP=1_000_000.0` (6 decimal places). Formula: `IDF = ln((N - df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5) + 1)`; `norm_factor = K1 * (1 - B + B * doc_len/avg_doc_len)`; `tf_norm = (tf*(K1+1))/(tf + norm_factor)`; final BM25 = sum over terms, then round6.

1156	```rust
1157	use crate::types::{CodeBlock, RankedBlock};
1158	
1159	pub fn dedup_blocks(blocks: Vec<RankedBlock>) -> Vec<RankedBlock> {
1160	    let mut result: Vec<RankedBlock> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());
1161	    'outer: for block in blocks {
1162	        for kept in &result {
1163	            if kept.block.file == block.block.file && overlaps_significantly(&kept.block, &block.block) {
1164	                continue 'outer;
1165	            }
1166	        }
1167	        result.push(block);
1168	    }
1169	    for (i, b) in result.iter_mut().enumerate() {
1170	        b.rank = i + 1;
1171	    }
1172	    result
1173	}
1174	
1175	fn overlaps_significantly(a: &CodeBlock, b: &CodeBlock) -> bool {
1176	    let overlap_start = a.line_start.max(b.line_start);
1177	    let overlap_end = a.line_end.min(b.line_end);
1178	    if overlap_start > overlap_end { return false; }
1179	    let overlap_lines = overlap_end - overlap_start + 1;
1180	    let smaller_len = (a.line_end - a.line_start + 1).min(b.line_end - b.line_start + 1);
1181	    overlap_lines * 2 > smaller_len
1182	}
1183	```
1184	
1185	Dedup rule: same file AND `overlap_lines * 2 > smaller_block_length` (i.e., >50% overlap of the smaller block). Input is assumed sorted desc by `final_score`; first kept wins. Ranks reassigned 1-based after dedup.

2736	use std::any::Any;

2740	
2741	pub fn run_napi<T, F, E>(f: F) -> napi::Result<T>
2742	where
2743	    F: FnOnce() -> Result<T, E>,
2744	    E: Error,
2745	{
2746	    match catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(f)) {
2747	        Ok(Ok(value)) => Ok(value),
2748	        Ok(Err(e)) => Err(flatten_error(&e)),
2749	        Err(payload) => Err(panic_payload_to_napi_error(&payload)),
2750	    }
2751	}
2752	
2753	pub async fn run_napi_async<T, F, Fut, E>(f: F) -> napi::Result<T>
2754	where
2755	    F: FnOnce() -> Fut,
2756	    Fut: core::future::Future<Output = Result<T, E>>,
2757	    E: Error,
2758	{
2759	    match f().await {
2760	        Ok(value) => Ok(value),
2761	        Err(e) => Err(flatten_error(&e)),
2762	    }
2763	}
2764	
2765	fn flatten_error(err: &dyn Error) -> napi::Error {
2766	    let mut msg = format!("{err}");
2767	    let mut source = err.source();
2768	    while let Some(s) = source {
2769	        let _ = write!(msg, "\n  caused by: {s}");
2770	        source = s.source();
2771	    }
2772	    napi::Error::from_reason(msg)
2773	}
2774	
2775	fn panic_payload_to_napi_error(payload: &Box<dyn Any + Send>) -> napi::Error {
2776	    let detail = payload
2777	        .downcast_ref::<&'static str>()
2778	        .copied()
2779	        .or_else(|| payload.downcast_ref::<String>().map(String::as_str))
2780	        .unwrap_or("(non-string panic payload)");
2781	    napi::Error::from_reason(format!(
2782	        "Rust panic caught at napi boundary: {detail} - this is a bug, please report"
2783	    ))
2784	}

2917	**Why not Probe (the reference pipeline):** binary-only (subprocess spawn ~30–50ms cold per call), tree-sitter (DX.Tools is OXC-standardized per ADR 0002), no persistent index (re-walks per invocation — unusable at 50k+ files), no stubhub-errors/camino/napi-boundary alignment.
2918	
2919	**What monokl keeps from Probe:** Pipeline shape (text prefilter → BM25 → dedup → budget) with substitutions: tree-sitter→OXC v0.128 + oxc_semantic; per-invocation walk→`FileAnalysis` cache + `WorkspaceIndex`; in-memory trigram→`grep-searcher` (ripgrep crates); PathBuf→Utf8PathBuf; anyhow→thiserror + FileIoError; tiktoken p50k_base→**o200k_base** (Claude/Sonnet).
2920	
2921	**Eight design tenets:**
2922	1. Parse once, use everywhere — single FileAnalysis cache feeds every tool.
2923	2. Aggregate views, not re-scans — ImportGraph/SymbolIndex folded from cached FileAnalysis.
2924	3. Token budget is non-negotiable — `max_bytes` 2MB hard ceiling, truncation marker required.
2925	4. Determinism — BTreeMap for serialized output; tie-break on (file, line_start); BM25 rounded to 6dp for cross-platform f64 stability.
2926	5. OXC arena lifetime containment (ADR 0002) — no `AstNode<'a>` escapes Allocator scope; all FileAnalysis fields are owned.
2927	6. Graceful degradation — broken file flips `had_parse_errors=true`, contributes recoverable data.
2928	7. Tier separation — Level 1 (per-file `LanguageAnalyzer`) co-produces; Level 2 (`WorkspaceEnricher`) folds.
2929	8. ContentHash is authoritative; mtime+size is the cheap fast-path dirty bit.
2930	
2931	**Non-goals:** full Salsa; C#/Roslyn in v1; tree-sitter; ts.LanguageService (dropped in TS 7.0); @typescript/api (Corsa IPC unstable until TS 7.1+); persistent on-disk search index (tantivy-style); agent loop; stemming; in-memory trigram index (removed in v4 — was 600MB–1.2GB).
2932	
2933	**Two-level architecture:**
2934	- Level 1 `LanguageAnalyzer` (one parse → FileAnalysis with symbols/dependencies/exports/blocks/JSX).
2935	- Level 2 `WorkspaceEnricher::update(idx, &FileAnalysis)` accumulates state; `finalize(self: Box<Self>, &mut WorkspaceIndex)` writes to the now-fully-populated index. Implementations: `ImportGraphEnricher`, `SymbolIndexEnricher`.
2936	
2937	**Two-tier cache invalidation:**
2938	1. `stat()` → if mtime+size matches → return cached (no file read).
2939	2. Else read file → blake3 ContentHash → if hash matches → refresh mtime/size, return cached.
2940	3. Else re-parse → cache.
2941	
2942	**Three-phase WorkspaceIndex::build:**
2943	1. Walk + parallel analyze via Rayon `par_iter()`, sort by `source_path` for stable `FileIdx`.
2944	2. Stream `enricher.update(idx, analysis)` for every (file, enricher) pair.
2945	3. `enricher.finalize(&mut index)` for each — at this point `file_index` is fully populated so `ImportGraphEnricher` can resolve `Utf8PathBuf → FileIdx`.
2946	4. Single atomic `persist::flush(root, config_hash)` at end (temp file + rename).
2947	
2948	**FileIdx invariants:** `pub(crate) struct FileIdx(pub(crate) u32)` — no Serialize derive (compile-time guard against leaking across rebuild boundaries); `u32` saves 4 bytes per edge vs `usize` (~16MB at 50k files).
2949	
2950	**Disk cache:** `<root>/.monokl/cache.json`; version=2; `config_hash` = `monokl-{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}-oxc-0.128-lang-ts-{tsconfig_blake3_or_'no-tsconfig'}` so monokl upgrade + tsconfig change both invalidate cache; size cap 100MB with LRU eviction in chunks of `(len/10).max(1)`.
2951	
2952	**Search pipeline stages (8):** Query Parse → Text Search (`grep-searcher` Aho-Corasick multi-pattern in one pass) → Boolean Eval (`+required` AND filter on hit lines; `-excluded` requires second pass over candidate set to check whole file) → Block Retrieval (analyze cache + matched-line filter) → BM25 Rank (K1=1.5, B=0.5, 6dp rounding) → Dedup (>50% line overlap within same file) → Token Budget (o200k_base BPE, 2MB hard ceiling) → SearchResponse.
2953	
2954	**BM25 tuning rationale:** K1=1.5, B=0.5 (Probe's code-search tuning). 6-decimal-place rounding before sort eliminates f64 FMA divergence between x86-64 CI and ARM64 dev machines.
2955	
2956	**Node-type boost rationale:** Functions are the most common search target (rank 1.5); class/method/constructor next (1.4); types (1.2–1.3); module 0.9; Other 0.7. Boost multiplies the BM25 score; coverage boost is additive.
2957	
2958	**LSP architecture (three-layer):** `LspSession` (wire protocol: `Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n` framing, NOT newline-delimited JSON; full `initialize`→`InitializeResult`→`initialized` handshake; circuit breaker — 3 crashes in 60s → 'tripped', 500ms backoff). `LanguageServerConfig` (per-language factory: `resolveServerPath`, `spawnArgs`, `rootUri`). `LspManager` (workspace router, lazy session start by extension).
2959	
2960	**LSP binary resolution:** Never PATH for npm-distributed servers — use `require.resolve('typescript-language-server/lib/cli.mjs')` and spawn node. PATH acceptable for `rustup`/`dotnet` (controlled toolchain managers). C# (`CSharpServerConfig`) deferred to ADR 0008 (proto-dotnet/orbit).
2961	
2962	**Language roadmap:** v1 = TypeScript/JavaScript (current — OXC + typescript-language-server). v1.1 = Rust (ra-ap-syntax + rust-analyzer) and Python (tree-sitter-python + pyright). v1.2 = C# (tree-sitter-c-sharp + OmniSharp/csharp-ls). Each slots into `LanguageAnalyzer` without changing the public NAPI API.
2963	
2964	**Latency targets at 50k files:** symbols(1 file) cold <50ms / warm <5ms / lite <5ms; dependents cold <15s / warm <30ms / lite <50ms; search(3-term) cold <15s / warm <300ms; WorkspaceIndex::build <15s cold; disk cache flush <800ms.
2965	
2966	**Per-file/total caps:**
2967	- symbols: 50 per file, 500 total (truncation marker `"[symbol cap 500 reached; pass fewer files or increase limit]"`).
2968	- dependents/imports: 200 each (marker `"[results capped at 200; {N} dependents, {M} imports total]"`).
2969	- search candidates: default 1000 (`SearchLimits::max_candidates`).
2970	- max_results default 50; max_tokens default 20000; max_bytes 2MB hard ceiling.
2971	
2972	**Query language:** Whitespace-separated terms; `+term` required, `-term` excluded, bare `term` optional (scored), `"exact phrase"` literal (escaped), `regex:pattern` raw regex. Max 64 terms (`MonoklError::TooManyTerms`). Default behavior tokenizes camelCase/snake_case; `--exact` skips tokenization and passes the full query as one escaped literal.
2973	
2974	**Test-path heuristic:** `is_test_path` excludes `/__tests__/`, `/test/`, `/tests/`, `/spec/` directories and `.test.ts`, `.test.tsx`, `.test.js`, `.spec.ts`, `.spec.tsx`, `.spec.js` extensions (unless `allow_tests=true`). Note: `.stories.tsx` is currently treated as production code.

3583	## `mnkl inspect` — Component inspection
3584	
3585	### Purpose
3586	
3587	Classify each input TypeScript/JavaScript (or Rust) file as one of: `react-component`, `react-hook`, `utility`, `type-module`, `test-file`, `story-file`, `config-module`, `barrel-module`, `context-module`, `panda-recipe`, `rust-struct`, `rust-enum`, `rust-trait`, `rust-module`, or `unknown`. Emits structured details for each.
3588	
3589	### InspectResult type verbatim
3590	
3591	```rust
3592	#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
3593	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
3594	pub struct InspectResult {
3595	    pub entries: Vec<InspectEntry>,
3596	    pub file_count: usize,
3597	    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
3598	}
3599	```

3600	
3601	### inspection.rs — algorithm verbatim
3602	
3603	Classification priority order (from `classify_analysis`):
3604	
3605	1. **StoryFile** — detected before TestFile/PandaRecipe. Detected by `*.stories.*` filename OR `deps.documentation.has_stories` OR a `@storybook/*` dependency.
3606	2. **ConfigModule** — `*.config.{ts|js|tsx|jsx|mts|cts|mjs|cjs}` filename. `config_kind` derived from filename stem against a known list (vite, panda, vitest, tailwind, next, jest, rollup, webpack, esbuild, postcss, eslint, prettier, tsup, storybook, svelte, astro, nuxt, remix) else `"unknown"`.
3607	3. **BarrelModule** — at least 2 re-exports AND ≥80% re-exports (`re_export_count * 5 >= total_exports * 4`).
3608	4. **PandaRecipe** — file contains a `defineRecipe`/`defineSlotRecipe`/`cva`/`sva` call (detected by `crate::panda::is_panda_recipe_file`). Multi-recipe files emit only the first with a `Warning` diagnostic naming the dropped count.
3609	5. **TestFile** — must run before ContextModule. Detected by non-empty `deps.test_utilities` OR `.test.`/`.spec.` filename OR `__tests__/` path component.
3610	6. **ContextModule** — detected after TestFile. Requires either a symbol signature containing `createContext(...)` (with optional `<…>` generics), OR a symbol whose owning block contains the call AND the file imports `createContext` from `react`/`react/*`.
3611	7. **ReactHook** — first symbol whose name starts with `use` AND fourth character is uppercase.
3612	8. **ReactComponent** — file has JSX elements AND first PascalCase symbol (kind Function/Variable/Class).
3613	9. **TypeModule** — non-empty symbols list where every symbol is an Interface/TypeAlias/Enum/Class.
3614	10. **Utility** — has any Function/Variable symbol.
3615	11. **Unknown** — fallback.
3616	
3617	Rust files (`.rs`) are routed to `crate::rust_inspection::inspect_rust_file` and bypass the TS analyzer entirely.
3618	
3619	Hook name detector:
3620	```rust
3621	fn is_hook_name(name: &str) -> bool {
3622	    if !name.starts_with("use") { return false; }
3623	    let mut chars = name.chars();
3624	    let _ = chars.next(); let _ = chars.next(); let _ = chars.next();
3625	    chars.next().is_some_and(char::is_uppercase)
3626	}
3627	```
3628	
3629	PascalCase detector:
3630	```rust
3631	fn is_pascal_case(name: &str) -> bool {
3632	    name.chars().next().is_some_and(char::is_uppercase)
3633	}
3634	```
3635	
3636	Type-module detector requires non-empty symbols where every symbol matches `Interface | TypeAlias | Enum | Class`.
3637	
3638	Test subject inference (`infer_subject_file`):
3639	- Strip `.test` / `.spec` from the file stem to recover the subject's bare stem.
3640	- If trimmed equals raw, abort (no recoverable subject).
3641	- Try sibling files in order: `<stem>.tsx`, `<stem>.ts`, `<stem>.jsx`, `<stem>.js`. Return the first that exists.
3642	- Fall back to scanning `deps.local` for matching basename — but only returns `None` if found (path not resolvable from import alone).
3643	
3644	Test count: number of code blocks whose code contains `it(`, `test(`, or `describe(`.
3645	
3646	Props extraction (`extract_props`):
3647	1. Find candidate prop type name (in order): from component param annotation; `<ComponentName>Props`; `<ComponentName>PropsType`; `Props`.
3648	2. Find matching `Interface` or `TypeAlias` symbol in `analysis.symbols`.
3649	3. Locate matching `CodeBlock` by `line_start == sym.line` and `node_kind == sym.kind` (or `SymbolKind::Other`).
3650	4. Extract the balanced `{...}` body and parse it with `parse_interface_fields` (splits on top-level `;`/`,`/`\n`, skipping `()`/`[]`/`{}` nested contexts; strips line and block comments; strips `readonly`; recognizes `name?: type`).
3651	5. Skip index signatures (`[k: string]: …`) and method shorthands (`foo(): void`).
3652	6. Falls back to a single placeholder field `(see TypeName)` when body can't be parsed.
3653	
3654	Pattern detection (`detect_component_patterns`):
3655	- Checks symbol signatures lowercased for `forwardref`, `memo(`/`react.memo`, `lazy(`/`react.lazy`.
3656	- Checks per-block code containing the component name.
3657	- Checks JSX elements containing `forwardref`.
3658	- `display_name` always `None` (placeholder for `Comp.displayName = "…"` detection).
3659	
3660	Used-hooks extractor (`extract_used_hooks`): scans owner's code blocks for `useXxx(` (where `xxx` starts with uppercase), preserves generic params (`useState<boolean>`), de-duplicates.
3661	
3662	Story meta extraction:
3663	- `find_meta_identifier_field`: locates `field:` in code, walks forward over an identifier (alpha/underscore/dollar then alnum/underscore/dollar/dot).
3664	- `find_meta_string_field`: locates `field:` then accepts a `"`, `'`, or backtick quote and returns the content up to the matching quote.
3665	- `extract_story_names`: every export except `default`, de-duplicated, source order preserved.
3666	
3667	Barrel re-export source counting (`count_reexport_source_files`): distinct re-export lines in `analysis.exports` AND distinct quoted specifiers from a textual `export … from '…'` scan — returns `max(from_lines, textual)`.
3668	
3669	HOC detection (`detect_is_hoc`): name starts with `with<Uppercase>` OR any symbol matches that shape OR component block contains `React.ComponentType` / `: ComponentType`.
3670	
3671	Lazy detection (`detect_react_lazy`): symbol signature contains `React.lazy` / `= lazy(` OR any block contains `React.lazy(` / `= lazy(` / ` lazy(`.
3672	
3673	Zod schema detection (`detect_zod_schemas`):
3674	1. Pre-check that file imports from `zod` or `@zod/core`.
3675	2. For each symbol with `signature_has_zod_call(sig)`, push name.
3676	3. Then for symbols not already pushed, check the block by `line_start == sym.line` and look for `z.<ident>(`.
3677	
3678	The `z.<ident>(` detector enforces word boundaries — `z` must not be part of a larger identifier.
3679	
3680	Empty result builders use `import_classifier::classify(&[])` for `empty_classified()`.
3681

3743	Algorithm (in `pipeline::patterns`):
3744	- Walks `dir` with `ignore::WalkBuilder` and `standard_filters(true)`.
3745	- Filters to files supported by `TsAnalyzer` (`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx`/`.mts`/`.cts`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`, excluding `.d.ts`).
3746	- Delegates to `inspection::inspect_files` for the entire batch.
3747	- First pass: iterate entries, tallying per-variant counters. For components, aggregates styling approach → count, pattern flags (forwardRef/memo/lazy) → count, hooks → `hooks_top`, props_style (interface if type_str contains `interface`, else type), export style label, and three-way test-coverage classification: `has_story` (has stories), `has_test` (no story but has test_utilities), `neither`.
3748	- For hooks/utilities/test-files, accumulates toolchain via `accumulate_toolchain`, state libs (BTreeSet), data fetching libs.
3749	- Second pass: per-component aggregates `hoc_count`, `lazy_count`, `zod_usage`, and `hooks_extended` for the four extended-hooks set `["useContext", "useReducer", "useMemo", "useSuspense"]` (matching after stripping generics — e.g. `useState<boolean>` strips to `useState`).
3750	- Utilities with non-empty `zod_schemas` also bump `zod_usage`.
3751	- Recipes collected from `InspectEntry::PandaRecipe` entries and aggregated via `crate::panda::aggregate_patterns(&recipes)`.

4019	   - **Imports**: iterate `analysis.dependencies` — match bindings where `imported == symbol` and kind is `Named` or `Default`, push `RefKind::Import` at `dep.line`.

4073	### definition.rs algorithm verbatim

4075	Constants:
4076	```rust

4078	const MAX_RE_EXPORT_HOPS: usize = 10;

4082

4084	2. `from_file` narrowing same as `refs` — resolve canonical source from importer.

4088	   - `kind = output_kind(sym.kind, &sym.name, is_jsx_file)`
4089	   - `signature = sym.signature.clone()`

4097	fn output_kind(kind: SymbolKind, name: &str, file_has_jsx: bool) -> &'static str {

4100	    }
4101	    if file_has_jsx
4102	        && is_pascal_case(name)
4103	        && matches!(kind, SymbolKind::Function | SymbolKind::Variable | SymbolKind::Class)
4104	    {
4105	        return "react-component";
4106	    }
4107	    symbol_kind_str(kind)

4110	fn symbol_kind_str(kind: SymbolKind) -> &'static str {
4111	    match kind {
4112	        SymbolKind::Function => "function",
4113	        SymbolKind::Class => "class",
4114	        SymbolKind::Interface => "interface",
4115	        SymbolKind::TypeAlias => "type",
4116	        SymbolKind::Enum => "enum",
4117	        SymbolKind::Variable => "const",

4124	Re-export chain walker (`resolve_re_export_chain`):
4125	- First hop: regex-scan `from_source` for the original re-export specifier (`find_re_export_specifier` tries `export\s*\{[^}]*\b{symbol}\b[^}]*\}\s*from\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]` then a wildcard `export\s*\*\s*from\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]`).

4206	3. For each change, `classify_file_kind(path, change_type)`:
4207	   - `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`/`__tests__/` → `"test"` (wins regardless).
4208	   - `.md`/`.mdx` → `"docs"`.
4209	   - `.github/` dir → `"chore"`.
4210	   - `.json`/`.toml`/`.yml`/`.yaml`/`.lock`/`.gitignore` → `"chore"`.
4211	   - Added: `/fix/` or `/bugfix/` path → `"fix"`; else `"feat"`.
4212	   - Deleted → `"refactor"`.
4213	   - Modified/Renamed: `/components/`, `/pages/`, `/views/` → `"feat"`; `/utils/`, `/helpers/`, `/lib/` → `"refactor"`; `fix` in name → `"fix"`; else `"refactor"`.

4215	5. Inspect happens against a tempfile that preserves the original extension (`write_temp_with_extension`).
4216	6. `diff_symbols(base, head)` extracts `(name, signature)` pairs from inspect entries via `symbols_of`:
4217	   - `ReactComponent` → `[(name, component_signature(c))]` where `component_signature(c) = format!("Component({})", props.iter().map(p.name).sorted().join(","))`.
4218	   - `ReactHook` → `[(name, hook_signature(h))]` where `hook_signature = format!("({}) -> {}", params.join(", "), returns.unwrap_or("void"))`.
4219	   - `Utility` → one entry per function with sig `(params) -> returns`.
4220	   - `TypeModule` → one entry per type with sig = type kind string.
4221	   - `PandaRecipe` → `[(name, "panda-recipe")]`.
4222	   - `RustStruct`/`RustEnum`/`RustTrait` → `[(name, "struct"|"enum"|"trait")]`.
4223	   - `Unknown` → all symbols with their signatures.
4224	   - `ContextModule` → context names with sig `"context"`.
4225	   - Test/Module/Story/Config/Barrel → empty.
4226	7. `diff_props` produces `props_added` / `props_removed` as `"name: type"` strings.
4227	8. `diff_imports` calls `scan_imports(src)` on each side, returns `BTreeSet<String>` symmetric diff in form `specifier::name` for named bindings, or bare `specifier` for default/namespace/side-effect.
4228	9. `compute_breaking_changes`:
4229	   - All `removed` symbols → breaking.
4230	   - `modified` symbols where `signature_change_is_breaking(before, after)`: `before_params > after_params` OR return clause changed.
4231	   - All `props_removed` → breaking, prefixed `prop:`.

4233	`scan_imports` parsers:
4234	- `parse_js_import_entries(line)`: handles `import "..."`, `import x from "..."`, `import { a, b as c } from "..."`, `import * as ns from "..."`, `import type { … }`. Each named binding emits `spec::name`.

4236	- `parse_python_import_entries`: `from spec import a, b` → `spec::a`, `spec::b`; `import spec` → `spec`.

4294	Constants:
4295	```rust
4296	const SEMANTIC_CATEGORIES: &[&str] = &[
4297	    "bg", "text", "border", "shadow", "fill", "stroke", "ring",
4298	    "colors", "spacing", "fontSizes", "fontWeights", "lineHeights",
4299	    "letterSpacings", "radii", "sizes", "zIndex",
4300	];
4301	
4302	const HARDCODED_NAMED_COLORS: &[&str] = &[
4303	    "red", "blue", "green", "white", "black", "transparent",
4304	    "yellow", "orange", "purple", "pink", "gray", "grey",
4305	];

4308	Algorithm (`audit_tokens`):
4309	1. `collect_source_files(dir)` — walk gitignore-aware, collect `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx`.
4310	2. For each file, read source, run `audit_file`:
4311	   - `styling_context_ranges(src)`: collect `[start, end)` byte ranges from both `RE_STYLING_CALL` (using `find_balanced` on `(`/`)`) and `RE_JSX_STYLE_PROP` (using `find_balanced` on inner `{`/`}`).
4312	   - For each range body, run `scan_hex_colors`, `scan_color_functions`, `scan_css_units`, `scan_named_colors`, `scan_primitive_tokens`, and `count_semantic_tokens`.
4313	3. `scan_css_units` skips zero dimensions via `value_is_zero_dimension(value)` (parses numeric prefix and rejects when 0).
4314	4. `scan_named_colors` only fires when the value is a string-literal exactly matching a `HARDCODED_NAMED_COLORS` entry (case-insensitive).
4315	5. `count_semantic_tokens` requires the literal value to match `RE_SEMANTIC_TOKEN` AND its first segment to be in `SEMANTIC_CATEGORIES`.

4317	7. Sort files by `file` ASC. Worst offenders: take top 5 files with non-empty hardcoded, sorted by `hardcoded.len()` DESC then file ASC.
4318	8. Overall: `overall_compliance = semantic / (semantic + hardcoded)`, falling to `1.0` when both zero. Primitives are not part of the denominator.

4320	Line/context translation:
4321	```rust
4322	fn line_and_context_for_offset(src: &str, offset: usize) -> (usize, String) {
4323	    let bytes = src.as_bytes();
4324	    let clamped = offset.min(bytes.len());
4325	    let line_start = src[..clamped].rfind('\n').map_or(0, |p| p + 1);
4326	    let line_end = src[clamped..].find('\n').map_or(bytes.len(), |p| clamped + p);
4327	    let line_number = bytecount_newlines(&src[..line_start]) + 1;
4328	    let raw_line = &src[line_start..line_end];
4329	    let trimmed = raw_line.trim();
4330	    let truncated: String = trimmed.chars().take(80).collect();
4331	    (line_number, truncated)
4332	}
4333	```

For `crate::…`: starts from `[]` and applies the tail segments. 5485 4. For `self::…`: starts from current_module. 5486 5. For `super::…`: pops one segment per leading `super`. 5487 6. For `extern_name::…`: first tries `resolve_module_path(&src_root, segments)` as a local sibling, then checks if `extern_name` equals the current crate name, and finally falls back to `package_roots.get(&normalized).join("src")` for cross-crate workspace resolution. 5488 7. Calls `resolve_module_path` which tries `{prefix}.rs` and `{prefix}/mod.rs` for each prefix length from the longest to the shortest. 5489 8. Falls back to `crate_entry_path(&src_root)` (`src/lib.rs` then `src/main.rs`) when only one segment remains. 5490 9. Final resolved path is returned only if `resolved.starts_with(&workspace_root_canon)` — workspace-boundary containment. 5491 5492 ### Fallback exports (when `lang-rs` not enabled) 5493 5494 ```rust 5495 #[cfg(not(feature = "lang-rs"))] 5496 fn extract_exports(source: &str) -> Vec { 5497 let mut exports = Vec::new(); 7907	# Part 4: Analysis Fidelity Slice (0.7.x — feat/monokl-analysis-fidelity-v2)
7908	
7909	> Added after Part 3. Closes the main semantic blind spots in the TypeScript and Rust analyzers.
7910	> No new commands; all changes are in `symbols` output fidelity.
7911	
7912	## Overview
7913	
7914	Two categories of work:
7915	
7916	1. **TypeScript signature normalization for variable-bound callables.** Arrow functions, function
7917	   expressions, and call-wrapped React exports assigned to a `const` now produce normalized
7918	   multi-line signatures instead of `None`.
7919	
7920	2. **Rust AST-based symbol extraction.** When `lang-rs` is enabled, `extract_symbols` uses the
7921	   `ra-ap-syntax` parse tree instead of the line scanner. The AST version adds normalized
7922	   signatures, correct visibility, `impl_owner`, and `trait_impl` fields.
7923	
7924	---
7925	
7926	## 1. Rust: AST-based `extract_symbols` (`#[cfg(feature = "lang-rs")]`)
7927	
7928	### What changed
7929	
7930	The `#[cfg(not(feature = "lang-rs"))]` line scanner (Part 3 §4) is now the fallback only.
7931	When parser support is compiled in, a parallel function takes the already-parsed `SourceFile`
7932	tree produced by `parse_with_profile`:
7933	
7934	```rust
7935	#[cfg(feature = "lang-rs")]
7936	fn extract_symbols(source: &str, tree: &SourceFile) -> Vec<SymbolEntry> {
7937	    let mut symbols = Vec::new();
7938	    for item in tree.items() {
7939	        extract_item_symbols(source, &item, &mut symbols);
7940	    }
7941	    symbols
7942	}
7943	```
7944	
7945	`extract_item_symbols` dispatches to `top_level_item_symbol` for named top-level items and, for
7946	`ast::Item::Impl`, also recurses into `extract_impl_symbols`.
7947	
7948	### `top_level_item_symbol`
7949	
7950	Handles: `Fn`, `Struct`, `Enum`, `Trait`, `Module`, `Const`, `Static`, `TypeAlias`, `MacroRules`.
7951	
7952	New item: `ast::Item::Static` emits `kind_detail = "rust-static"` (not present in the line
7953	scanner).
7954	
7955	Each arm calls:
7956	
7957	```rust
7958	ast_symbol(
7959	    source,
7960	    node.syntax(),
7961	    node.name().map(|n| n.text().to_string()),
7962	    SymbolKind::Function,          // or Struct, Enum, etc.
7963	    "rust-function",               // or "rust-struct", etc.
7964	    rust_visibility(node.syntax()),
7965	    rust_signature(source, node.syntax(), Some(SyntaxKind::L_CURLY)),
7966	)
7967	```
7968	
7969	**`rust_visibility(node)`** — walks the node's children for a `Visibility` token and maps
7970	`pub`, `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, `pub(self)` to `Visibility::{Public, Crate, Super, Module}`.
7971	Defaults to `Visibility::Private` when absent.
7972	
7973	**`rust_signature(source, node, stop_before)`** — slices the raw source from the node's start
7974	offset to just before the first occurrence of `stop_before` token kind (`L_CURLY` for
7975	fn/struct/enum/trait/mod/impl, `EQ` for const/static/type). Multi-line slices are flattened by
7976	collapsing inner whitespace runs to a single space. Leading attribute tokens (`#[...]`) are
7977	excluded by advancing past the last attribute child before the slice.
7978	
7979	### `extract_impl_symbols`
7980	
7981	`impl` blocks emit one `SymbolEntry` for the `impl` itself plus one per associated `fn`. The
7982	impl-level symbol carries:
7983	
7984	- `name` — the self type as text (e.g., `Widget<T>`).
7985	- `kind_detail` — `"rust-impl"`.
7986	- `impl_owner` — `Some(self_ty_text)`.
7987	- `trait_impl` — `Some(trait_name)` when the `impl` has a `for` clause (e.g.,
7988	  `impl Render for Widget<T>` → `trait_impl = Some("Render")`).
7989	
7990	Each associated `fn` inside the impl carries:
7991	- `impl_owner` — the parent impl's self type (propagated down).
7992	- `trait_impl` — the parent impl's trait name if present.
7993	- `kind_detail` — `"rust-function"`.
7994	
7995	### New `kind_detail` values
7996	
7997	| `kind_detail`   | Source item                        | New in v2 |
7998	|-----------------|------------------------------------|-----------|
7999	| `"rust-impl"`   | `impl Foo` / `impl Trait for Foo`  | ✅        |
8000	| `"rust-static"` | `static FOO: T = ...`              | ✅        |
8001	
8002	All others (`"rust-struct"`, `"rust-enum"`, `"rust-trait"`, `"rust-function"`, `"rust-type"`,
8003	`"rust-const"`, `"rust-module"`) existed in the line scanner. The AST version adds correct
8004	signatures and visibility to them.
8005	
8006	### Tests added

8008	```rust

8012	    // Source: pub(crate) struct Widget<T>, pub trait Render,
8013	    //   impl<T> Widget<T> { pub fn new }, impl<T: Display> Render for Widget<T> { fn render }
8014	    // Asserts:
8015	    //   Widget → visibility = Crate, signature = "pub(crate) struct Widget<T>"
8016	    //   new → impl_owner = Some("Widget<T>"), trait_impl = None
8017	    //   render → impl_owner = Some("Widget<T>"), trait_impl = Some("Render")

8023	## 2. TypeScript: variable-bound callable signatures
8024	
8025	### What changed
8026	
8027	`extract_stmt` and `extract_export_decl` previously emitted `signature: None` for
8028	`VariableDeclarator` nodes where the initializer was a function-like expression. Both now call:
8029	
8030	```rust
8031	signature: declarator
8032	    .init
8033	    .as_ref()
8034	    .and_then(|init| variable_function_signature(source, declarator.span.start, init)),
8035	```
8036	
8037	### `variable_function_signature`
8038	
8039	```rust
8040	fn variable_function_signature(source: &str, start: u32, init: &Expression<'_>) -> Option<String> {
8041	    match init {
8042	        Expression::ArrowFunctionExpression(arrow) => {
8043	            normalize_signature(&source[start as usize..arrow.body.span().start as usize])
8044	        }
8045	        Expression::FunctionExpression(func) => function_signature(
8046	            source,
8047	            start,
8048	            func.body.as_ref().map(|body| body.span.start),
8049	            init.span().end,
8050	        ),
8051	        Expression::CallExpression(call) => {
8052	            let body_start = call
8053	                .arguments
8054	                .first()
8055	                .and_then(|arg| arg.as_expression())
8056	                .and_then(wrapped_function_body_start)?;
8057	            normalize_signature(&source[start as usize..body_start as usize])
8058	        }
8059	        _ => None,
8060	    }
8061	}
8062	```
8063	
8064	`start` is `declarator.span.start` — the slice covers the full `const Widget = …` up to the
8065	body brace (or arrow body), so the signature includes the LHS name.
8066	
8067	### `wrapped_function_body_start`
8068	
8069	Recursively unwraps nested call expressions to find the innermost function-like argument:
8070	
8071	```rust
8072	fn wrapped_function_body_start(expr: &Expression<'_>) -> Option<u32> {
8073	    match expr {
8074	        Expression::ArrowFunctionExpression(arrow) => Some(arrow.body.span().start),
8075	        Expression::FunctionExpression(func) => func.body.as_ref().map(|body| body.span.start),
8076	        Expression::CallExpression(call) => call
8077	            .arguments
8078	            .first()
8079	            .and_then(|arg| arg.as_expression())
8080	            .and_then(wrapped_function_body_start),
8081	        _ => None,
8082	    }
8083	}
8084	```
8085	
8086	This handles arbitrarily nested wrappers: `memo(forwardRef(connect(mapState)(fn)))` would
8087	recurse through each call's first argument until it hits a function expression or arrow.
8088	
8089	### Shapes covered
8090	
8091	| Input shape | Normalized signature |
8092	|---|---|
8093	| `const Widget = (props: P): JSX.Element => {` | `Widget = (props: P): JSX.Element =>` |
8094	| `const Widget = function(props: P): JSX.Element {` | `Widget = function(props: P): JSX.Element` |
8095	| `const Widget = memo(forwardRef<Div, P>((props, ref): JSX.Element => {` | `Widget = memo(forwardRef<Div, P>((props, ref): JSX.Element =>` |
8096	
8097	Multi-line forms collapse inner whitespace to a single space via `normalize_signature` (already
8098	used for `FunctionDeclaration` signatures — same normalization path).
8099	
8100	### Shapes NOT covered (intentional)
8101	
8102	`export default function() {}` / `export default () =>` / `export default class extends C {}` —
8103	anonymous default exports. These are future work requiring an explicit output-contract decision
8104	on synthetic naming. See strategic-roadmap.md §Analysis Fidelity.
8105	
8106	### Tests added (in `integration_new_commands.rs`)
8107	
8108	Three new black-box tests against the compiled binary:
8109	
8110	- `symbols_multiline_arrow_function_variable_signature_is_normalized` — arrow function form.
8111	- `symbols_multiline_function_expression_variable_signature_is_normalized` — function expression form.
8112	- `symbols_wrapped_call_expression_variable_signature_is_normalized` — `memo(forwardRef(...))` form.
8113	
8114	---
8115	
8116	## 3. Python — fidelity considerations for v1.1
8117	
8118	Python is slated for v1.1 (`lang-py`, tree-sitter-python, pyright). Its fidelity challenges
8119	differ substantially from TypeScript and Rust.
8120	
8121	### Non-problems (Python eliminates these)
8122	
8123	- **Anonymous default exports** — Python has no `export default`. `def` and `class` always bind
8124	  a name. The synthetic-naming decision (§TS above) does not apply.
8125	- **Multiline variable-bound lambdas** — Python `lambda` is syntactically single-expression.
8126	  Multi-line callable definitions always use `def`, which always produces a named symbol.
8127	- **Call-wrapped anonymous exports** — extremely rare at module level. `def` preserves the name
8128	  through any decoration context.
8129	
8130	### Python-specific fidelity problems that DO matter
8131	
8132	**1. `__init__.py` re-export attribution.**
8133	The common "package as API" pattern:
8134	```python
8135	# mylib/__init__.py
8136	from .button import Button
8137	from .input import Input
8138	__all__ = ["Button", "Input"]
8139	```
8140	`mnkl symbols mylib/__init__.py` should attribute `Button` and `Input` to their origin files,
8141	not emit them as new symbols defined here. Analogous to `pub use` re-export attribution in Rust.
8142	
8143	**2. Decorator effects on signature.**
8144	Decorators change the effective calling signature:
8145	```python
8146	@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
8147	def expensive(x: int) -> str: ...   # effective signature unchanged here
8148	
8149	@property
8150	def host(self) -> str: ...          # becomes a getter descriptor
8151	
8152	@app.route("/users")
8153	async def list_users(req): ...      # becomes a route handler
8154	```
8155	The symbol should carry both the declared signature and a `decorator` field listing applied
8156	decorators, so consumers can reason about the effective calling shape. Analogous to
8157	`trait_impl` on Rust symbols marking behavioral enrichment.
8158	
8159	**3. `__all__`-based visibility.**
8160	Python has no enforced access control. The effective public API is:
8161	- Names in `__all__` (when present) — explicitly exported.
8162	- Names not prefixed with `_` (when `__all__` absent) — conventionally public.
8163	- Names prefixed with `_` — conventionally private.
8164	`visibility` in Python `symbols` output should map: `__all__` member → `Public`, `_`-prefixed →
8165	`Private`, otherwise `Module` (file-scoped public convention).
8166	
8167	**4. Protocol implementations.**
8168	```python
8169	class Foo(Protocol):    # defines a protocol — analogous to trait
8170	    def bar(self) -> int: ...
8171	
8172	class Widget(Foo):      # structural impl — analogous to impl Trait for Foo
8173	    def bar(self) -> int: return 42
8174	```
8175	`symbols` should carry `protocol_impl: Option<String>` on implementors, parallel to
8176	`trait_impl` on Rust symbols.
8177	
8178	**5. Type annotation resolution.**
8179	`from __future__ import annotations` makes all annotations lazy strings at runtime.
8180	Getting correct signatures without a type-checker (pyright/mypy) integration requires resolving
8181	forward references, which is approximate. The spec for `lang-py` should declare this as
8182	`CapabilityPrecision::Approximate` on `inspect_detail` until pyright integration lands.
8183	
8184	**6. `@property` / `@classmethod` / `@staticmethod` tagging.**
8185	These three decorators change calling semantics enough that `mnkl symbols` should tag them
8186	explicitly — `kind_detail` values: `"py-property"`, `"py-classmethod"`, `"py-staticmethod"`.
8187	Plain methods are `"py-method"`. Module-level functions are `"py-function"`.
8188	
8189	### Proposed Python `kind_detail` values
8190	
8191	| `kind_detail`        | Python item                              |
8192	|----------------------|------------------------------------------|
8193	| `"py-function"`      | module-level `def`                       |
8194	| `"py-async-function"`| module-level `async def`                 |
8195	| `"py-class"`         | `class`                                  |
8196	| `"py-method"`        | method inside a class                    |
8197	| `"py-classmethod"`   | `@classmethod` method                    |
8198	| `"py-staticmethod"`  | `@staticmethod` method                   |
8199	| `"py-property"`      | `@property` getter                       |
8200	| `"py-const"`         | module-level name in ALL_CAPS (convention)|
8201	
8202	These are forward-planning values, not yet implemented. They should be locked in the spec
8203	before the `lang-py` feature branch starts to avoid symbol output breaking changes mid-PR.

<result># CodeGraph: Analysis & Comparison to Monokl

## 1. What CodeGraph Is

**CodeGraph** (`@colbymchenry/codegraph`, MIT, v1.4.1/1.0 released) is a mature, production TypeScript CLI + embeddable library + MCP server. Positioning is explicit and narrow: *"Supercharge AI coding agents with semantic code intelligence — surgical context, fewer tool calls, faster answers. 100% local."* — human use is secondary; the README's benchmark section frames everything around agent tool-call/token/cost reduction.

**Architecture** (`CLAUDE.md:36-64`):
```
files → ExtractionOrchestrator (tree-sitter) → SQLite (nodes/edges/files, FTS5)
      → ReferenceResolver (imports, name-matching, framework patterns)
      → GraphTraverser/GraphQueryManager (callers/callees/impact)
      → ContextBuilder (markdown/JSON for AI consumption)
```
- **Parsing**: `web-tree-sitter` + `tree-sitter-wasms` (WASM grammars, no native compile step) across 30+ languages, one extractor file per language (`src/extraction/languages/*.ts`), plus hand-written extractors for non-tree-sitter formats (Svelte/Vue/Liquid/Delphi).
- **Storage**: real SQLite via Node's built-in `node:sqlite`, with `nodes`/`edges`/`files`/`unresolved_refs` tables (`src/db/schema.sql`), FTS5 full-text index with triggers, and SQLite's **built-in `bm25()`** ranking function used directly (`src/db/queries.ts:1389`: `bm25(nodes_fts, 0, 20, 5, 1, 2)`).
- **Resolution**: cross-file reference resolution with a retry queue — `unresolved_refs` rows persist as `pending`/`failed` and are retried on subsequent syncs rather than requiring a full reparse (`schema.sql` comments above that table).
- **Sync**: a background daemon + native FS watcher (FSEvents/inotify/RDCW) debounces edits (2s default) and auto-reindexes; MCP responses prepend a "⚠️ stale" banner for files still in the debounce window (`README.md` "How auto-syncing works").
- **MCP surface**: deliberately **one primary tool**, `codegraph_explore` — other tools (`node`, `search`, `callers`, `callees`, `impact`, `files`, `status`) exist but are unlisted by default because "one strong tool steers agents better than a menu of narrower ones" (`README.md` "MCP Tools"; rationale documented at length in `CLAUDE.md:98-134`).
- **Extras**: framework-aware route detection (17 frameworks → `route` nodes), cross-language bridge synthesis (Swift↔ObjC, RN bridge, Expo), all synthesized edges tagged `provenance:'heuristic'` + `metadata.synthesizedBy` for traceability.
- Ships real benchmarks: 7 open-source repos, headless Claude-Code A/B, median of 4 runs, tracking tool calls/time/tokens/cost (`README.md:185-310`, harness at `__tests__/evaluation/runner.ts`, `docs/benchmarks/call-sequence-analysis.md`).

## 2. Head-to-Head

| Dimension | CodeGraph | Monokl (spec) |
|---|---|---|
| Index persistence | Persistent SQLite + FTS5, daemon-synced | Explicitly no persistent index (non-goal); in-memory recompute + `.monokl/cache.json` for parsed data |
| Ranking | SQLite's built-in `bm25()` over FTS5 | Custom BM25 (K1/B tuned) over ripgrep prefilter — more control, no DB dependency |
| Parsing | tree-sitter (WASM), generic queries, 30+ languages, 1 extractor file each | oxc (native, type-aware) for TS/JS, ra-ap-syntax for Rust — deeper precision, far fewer languages |
| Freshness | Push-based: FS watcher + debounce + staleness banners | Pull-based: stat/blake3 cache check on each invocation |
| Agent tool surface | 1 primary MCP tool by design (empirically validated) | ~20 CLI commands, each schema'd separately |
| Query language | Field filters (`kind:`, `lang:`, `path:`, `name:`) + free text to FTS | `+req`/`-excl`/phrase/`regex:`, boolean/grep-like |
| Output contracts | Boolean `--json`, no schema versioning | JSON Schema per result type, `--only`/`--fields` projection |
| Graceful degradation | None documented — languages either supported or not | `AnalyzerCapabilities` (Unsupported/Heuristic/Structural/Exact) |
| PR/git-scoping | One narrow command (`affected`, import-reachability to tests) | General git-scope model (FullRepo/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines/ImpactedNeighbors) applicable to any command |
| Provenance | Per-edge `provenance`/`synthesizedBy` tags | Per-analyzer/operation precision level (coarser) |
| Evaluation | Real headless-agent A/B benchmarks, checked into repo | Not mentioned in spec |
| Distribution | Bundled Node runtime, installers, signed/attested releases | Native Rust binary — already simpler/faster to distribute |

## 3. Recommendations for Monokl

1. **Adopt the "sufficiency, not menu" tool-design principle.** CodeGraph's own experiments (`CLAUDE.md:98-134`) showed that adding narrow tools or "steering" instructions doesn't move agent behavior — only a tool whose single response is *complete enough to stop the agent reading* does. Monokl's `explain` (inspect+refs+dependents) is the right instinct; when an MCP server is built, expose one or two composite tools by default (e.g., `explain`, `search`) and keep the ~20 granular commands as CLI/unlisted-MCP fallbacks, not the primary agent-facing surface.

2. **Add per-edge provenance tagging**, not just per-analyzer capability levels. `edges.provenance` + `synthesizedBy` (schema.sql) lets an agent see *how* a hop got into the graph. Monokl's `WorkspaceIndex` import graph should tag synthesized/heuristic edges (e.g., dynamic `require()`, re-export chains) the same way — cheap to add, high trust value.

3. **Build an eval harness now, not later.** Monokl's BM25 tuning (K1=1.5, B=0.5) and token-budget design are currently unvalidated assumptions. Copy CodeGraph's methodology: headless agent A/B on real repos, median-of-N, measuring tool calls/tokens/wall-clock — cheap to build, and it's the only way to know if the ranking pipeline actually helps.

4. **Reconsider the "no persistent index" non-goal, at least partially.** SQLite+FTS5 (or a lighter embedded equivalent) gives O(log n) symbol/text lookup without reparsing, and the `unresolved_refs` retry-queue pattern (persist failed cross-file resolutions, retry only those on next sync) is more surgical than monokl's blanket cache-hash invalidation. Even without a full DB, adopt the retry-queue idea for `ImportGraphEnricher`.

5. **Explicit staleness disclosure.** If monokl ever runs as a long-lived MCP process, borrow the "⚠️ pending sync" banner pattern rather than silently serving cache-stale results.

6. **Framework-aware route/entrypoint enrichment** is a concrete, high-value `WorkspaceEnricher` to add for JS (Express/Next.js routes) given monokl's two-level architecture already anticipates pluggable enrichers.

Where monokl is already ahead: JSON Schema per result + field projection, general git-scope composability across *all* commands (vs. codegraph's one-off `affected`), and capability-driven graceful degradation — none of these exist in codegraph today.

<result>## CodeGraph Deep-Dive: Implementation-Level Findings

**Scope read in full (not grepped):** `src/extraction/index.ts` (2714 lines), `src/extraction/languages/typescript.ts` + `python.ts`, `src/db/schema.sql` (195 lines), relevant sections of `src/db/queries.ts` (2432 lines), `src/resolution/index.ts` (2000 lines, read to line 1234+), `src/graph/traversal.ts` (733 lines, full), `src/context/index.ts` (structure + key methods), `src/mcp/tools.ts` (targeted: `handleExplore` at line 2502+), `src/sync/watcher.ts` (debounce/flush logic), `src/sync/watch-policy.ts` (full, 105 lines).

### Extraction orchestrator (`src/extraction/index.ts`)
`ExtractionOrchestrator.indexAll` (line 1507) is a genuinely sophisticated pipeline, not a naive loop: files are read in I/O batches of 10 (`FILE_IO_BATCH_SIZE`, line 41), dispatched into a **bounded rolling window** over a `ParseWorkerPool` (worker_threads, sized `clamp(cores-1,1,8)`), but committed to SQLite in strict **original file order** via a `completed: Map<seq,…>` + `flushOrdered()` promise chain (lines 1673–1817) — because later reference resolution disambiguates same-named candidates by DB insertion order, and out-of-order commits would make results non-deterministic (explicitly documented, #1015). Parse errors don't crash the run: failures are caught per-file (line 1798), recorded with `code: 'parse_error'`, and a **retry pass** re-parses on a freshly recycled worker (WASM heap can't shrink, so workers are recycled every 250 files — line 72), and a *second* retry strips comment-only lines for files that still crash (lines 1998–2047) — a real, hand-built defense against tree-sitter WASM memory exhaustion on huge files. This is meaningfully more engineered than "parse and catch."

### Language extractors
There are **no `.scm` tree-sitter query files anywhere in the repo** (`find . -name '*.scm'` → empty). Extraction is a single ~6700-line generic AST-walking engine (`TreeSitterExtractor` class, `src/extraction/tree-sitter.ts:389`) driven by declarative per-language config objects (`LanguageExtractor` interface — `functionTypes`, `classTypes`, `nameField`, `resolveBody`, etc., e.g. `typescript.ts:41`). This is "generic core + per-language hooks," not "generic core, no hooks": there are 28 inline `language === '…'`/`lang === '…'` branches still inside the "generic" engine, and the TS extractor alone hand-codes arrow-function class-field detection, HOF-wrapper unwrapping (`throttle(() => {...})`), and export-statement ancestor walking (`typescript.ts:16-38,56-84,109-120`). Every `calls`/`extends`/`import` reference becomes an `UnresolvedReference` pushed to an array (69 call sites of `unresolvedReferences.push` in `tree-sitter.ts`) — extraction never resolves anything itself; it's a pure two-phase design (local syntactic pass → later global resolution pass).

### Schema (`src/db/schema.sql`)
Fully normalized `nodes`/`edges`/`files` core, `edges` has an explicit `UNIQUE(source,target,kind,IFNULL(line,-1),IFNULL(col,-1))` index (line 173-174) added specifically to fix duplicate-edge inflation (#1034) — `insertEdge` uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` against it. FTS5 (`nodes_fts`, `content='nodes'`, external-content mode) is kept in sync via three triggers (`nodes_ai/ad/au`, lines 119-134) doing the delete+reinsert dance FTS5 external-content requires. `unresolved_refs` (lines 79-92) genuinely implements a status lifecycle: rows insert `status='pending'`; a completed resolution pass either **deletes** the row (resolved, `deleteReferencesByRowIds`/`deleteSpecificResolvedReferences` in `resolution/index.ts:1086-1087`) or **marks it `'failed'`** with a computed `name_tail` (`markReferencesFailedByRowIds`/`markReferencesFailed`, line 1101-1102) so a later `sync` can retry it when a new file introduces a matching symbol (#1240). Rows are keyed by row-id where possible specifically to avoid a documented bug (#1269) where key-tuple deletes would wrongly flip sibling call-sites of the same name.

### Query layer (`src/db/queries.ts`)
Real parameterized prepared statements throughout — every value goes through `.prepare(sql).all(...params)` with `?` placeholders; the only string-built parts are `?`-placeholder repetition for `IN (...)` clauses sized to array length, never value interpolation. **No SQL injection risk observed.** The BM25 call is explicit and hand-weighted: `SELECT nodes.*, bm25(nodes_fts, 0, 20, 5, 1, 2) as score ...` (`queries.ts:1389`) — column weights `id=0, name=20, qualified_name=5, docstring=1, signature=2`, over-fetching `limit*5` rows (line 1386) specifically so a post-hoc rescoring pass (kind bonus, path relevance, name-match bonus) can override BM25's ranking downstream. There's also a separate Levenshtein-ish fuzzy fallback (`sql = 'SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE name = ?'`-based, line 1330+) and a `LIKE`-based fallback (line 1426) for camelCase substring matches FTS5's tokenizer misses.

### Reference resolver (`src/resolution/index.ts`)
Not a formal scope-aware symbol table, but far more than name-matching: `resolveOne` (line 770) runs a **strategy cascade** — hardcoded language built-in sets (JS/Python/Go/C/C++/Pascal built-ins, lines 72-197), a `hasAnyPossibleMatch` pre-filter against a cached name-set, then framework resolvers, then real **import-graph resolution** (`resolveViaImport`, parses actual import statements) at confidence ≥0.9 short-circuit, then JVM FQN resolution via exact qualified-name lookup (unambiguous even with duplicate simple names), then a fuzzy `matchReference` fallback, each candidate carrying a confidence score with highest-confidence-wins arbitration (lines 916-946). Chained/fluent calls (`Foo.builder().method()`) that fail get deferred to a **second pass** (`resolveChainedCallsViaConformance`, line 1164) that runs only after `implements`/`extends` edges exist, walking supertype conformance. There are 20+ framework-specific resolvers (`src/resolution/frameworks/*.ts` — Express, NestJS, Laravel, Spring, Vue, React Native bridges, Terraform, etc.), each hardcoded to that framework's idioms. This is a heuristic, confidence-ranked system with real import-parsing as its most precise tier — not a compiler-grade binder, but well beyond naive string matching.

### Graph traversal (`src/graph/traversal.ts`, read in full)
`GraphTraverser` implements textbook BFS (`traverseBFS`) and recursive DFS with explicit `visited`/`enqueued` sets, per-node depth limits, and hard result-size caps checked at *every* add site (not just loop tops) — three separate documented bugfixes (#1086, #1087, #1088, #1089, #1090) show these caps/visited-orderings were each individually broken and fixed, evidence of real production hardening under load. `getImpactRadius` explicitly excludes `contains` edges from the "affects" direction to avoid impact explosion through sibling class members (#536) while still recursing *into* container children to catch method-level callers. All neighbor fetches are batched (`getNodesByIds`) to eliminate N+1 query patterns, called out in comments as deliberate perf fixes.

### MCP `codegraph_explore` (`src/mcp/tools.ts:2502`)
Traces cleanly: `handleExplore` → `cg.findRelevantContext()` (context builder, BM25+traversal) → a **"glue" pass** pulling in callers/callees of root nodes restricted to files already in the subgraph (lines 2546-2568) → a large "named-symbol seeding" heuristic block (2579-2680+) that re-resolves query tokens directly against symbol names to compensate for FTS ranking failures on multi-term queries. Tool visibility itself is gated by empirical A/B results baked into comments (`tools.ts:980-1005`): a 3-tool gate "regressed on cobra/ky/sinatra," a 1-tool gate caused "+107% LOSS" on express — real evaluation-driven tuning, cited by repo name.

### Watcher/staleness (`src/sync/watcher.ts`)
Debounce is a simple `setTimeout` reset (`scheduleSync`, line 767-775) but the staleness tracking is carefully race-proof: `pendingFiles` entries are only cleared after a successful sync **and** only if `lastSeenMs <= syncStartedMs` (line 822-826), explicitly preferring false-positive staleness over false-negative (documented rationale, lines 815-821). Lock contention gets exponential backoff (`scheduleRetrySync`) separate from normal debounce. `watch-policy.ts` disables the watcher entirely on WSL2 `/mnt/*` drives because recursive `fs.watch` there is too slow (#199) — a real-world edge case, not theoretical.

### Honest assessment
This is **production-grade, not a fast prototype.** Evidence: `resolution.test.ts` alone is ~5000 lines; only 7 TODO/FIXME/HACK comments in the entire `src/`; nearly every non-obvious code path has a comment citing a specific GitHub issue number describing the bug it fixes (dozens observed: #1015, #1034, #1086-1090, #1231, #1240, #1269, #199, #536...), indicating an actively-maintained tool responding to real production failures rather than greenfield design. The reference resolver and explore-tool ranking are heavily heuristic and increasingly complex (accumulating special cases like `#1064`, `#1196`, `#720` in `handleExplore`) — this is the clearest technical-debt smell: correctness by accretion of corpus-specific tuning rather than a principled model, which is exactly the gap a real symbol-table/scope resolver (as monokl could build with ra-ap-syntax/OXC) could close with more precision and less bespoke logic.</result>
